confirmed.statement: (a) The Methods state random assignment of individuals after recruitment and consent: 'Then they were randomly assigned to either the experimental or the control group, each comprising 40 students.' The form's assignment quote and locator are verbatim and correct. In the text layer of all 30 PDF pages, the only other 'random' is the selection of 18 interviewees from the experimental group.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, Methodology, Participants; PDF p. 10, Procedure step (4); search of the PDF text layer, pp. 1-30, for 'random'

confirmed.statement: (a) The form records the counter-evidence correctly. The paper calls its design quasi-experimental three times: 'We used quasi-experiments' (Abstract), 'A quasi-experimental approach was taken' (Introduction), and 'This study adopted a quasi-experimental approach' (Procedure). It gives no randomization method. It argues comparability from the participants' shared first semester ('This suggests they possessed comparable baseline learning backgrounds and practical competencies'), and it prints no pretest means or baseline test. No page mentions intact classes, cohorts, self-selection into arms, matching, stratification, or an allocation procedure. The label is the only signal against the Methods sentence, so randomized = yes records what the paper states, and eligibility.reason and open_questions flag the conflict.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 1, Abstract; p. 3, Introduction; p. 8, Participants and Procedure; p. 13, Data analysis; p. 20, Table 7; search of the PDF text layer, pp. 1-30, for 'quasi', 'intact', 'cohort', 'self-select', 'allocat', 'match', 'stratif', 'balanc', 'lottery'

confirmed.statement: unit = individual and structure = between are supported. The sentence assigns the participants ('they'), not classes or pairs. Each student stayed in one group for the whole study, September through December, and Fig. 1 shows two parallel five-step sequences. The PDF has no crossover, within-subject, or order-of-conditions language, so check (e) does not apply.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, Participants and Fig. 1; search of the PDF text layer, pp. 1-30, for 'cross-over', 'within-subject', 'within-person', 'counterbalanc', 'order'

confirmed.statement: preregistered = not_stated is right. No page mentions a preregistration, a trial registry, or OSF. The declarations cover voluntary participation, informed consent, and withdrawal, and they name no ethics committee or registration.
confirmed.locator: search of the PDF text layer, pp. 1-30, for 'regist' and 'OSF'; PDF p. 27, Declarations

confirmed.statement: (b) What was assigned is a generative-AI dialogue partner for the participant's own work. Students in the experimental group 'were asked to use the app Dou Bao and undertake dialogue exchanges with it to achieve the goal of creating an innovative and practical research proposal'. Both groups then submitted 'a new research proposal based on the discussions undertaken with either Dou Bao or a peer', and two markers scored each one. The arms differ in the dialogue partner, not only in whose output is evaluated.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Procedure step (3); p. 10, Procedure step (5); p. 12, Measures of students' practical competencies in CPS

confirmed.statement: (c) The tool is generative AI. 'Dou Bao is a GAI chatbot developed by ByteDance', and 'Similar to ChatGPT, the Dou Bao chatbot operates by relying on large language models'. The paper gives no model version, as name_model says. Students talked with it by text or speech inside themed sessions, so role open_chat fits. An interviewee says the chatbot 'could even outline a research design', so it supplied content and was not a coach.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Procedure step (3); p. 19, RQ2 interview excerpts; codebook section 6, AI role

confirmed.statement: (d) The comparison arm matches the form. Each control student 'was asked to choose one peer for dialogue interaction', with the same goal as the experimental group, and 'the control group did not have access to other similar tools during the study period'. ai = other_aid fits the form spec, which puts human partners under other_aid, and an AI-versus-human-partner contrast is ai_vs_active in codebook section 5.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, Participants; p. 9, Procedure step (3); form-spec.md, field note on arms[].ai; codebook section 5

confirmed.statement: The arm descriptions match the Procedure. All participants had one three-hour training session. Both groups had five interactions, one per week, each designed to last half an hour, on the research topic, research questions, literature, research design, and originality. The exchanges were audio-recorded and transcribed, and each student then submitted a new proposal. Fig. 1 shows the same five steps for both groups.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, Fig. 1; p. 9, Procedure steps (2) and (3); p. 10, step (5)

confirmed.statement: Arm counts match. The assignment sentence gives 'each comprising 40 students', and Table 7 gives N = 40 per group, so n_randomized = n_analyzed = 40 per arm for the proposal score. The paper reports no attrition or exclusion for that outcome. The N = 36 per group of the perception survey (Table 6) does not affect the assignment fields.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, Participants; p. 20, Table 7; p. 19, Table 6

confirmed.statement: The paper does not say who the control students' peers were or whether any of them were study participants, as open_questions says. A peer from the experimental group could carry chatbot content into the control arm. This is a risk of contamination, not an error in the coded fields.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, Introduction; p. 8, Participants; p. 9, Procedure step (3)

confirmed.statement: design_class lies outside this lens. field_rct and lab_rct are both randomized codes. The paper does not say whether the new proposal counted toward coursework or the degree, so the form is right to leave the choice between them open.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 8-10, Participants and Procedure; codebook section 4

summary: The PDF supports every assignment, arm, and tool field: the Methods say the 80 volunteer PhD students 'were randomly assigned' as individuals, 40 and 40, to five weekly dialogue sessions with Dou Bao, a ByteDance chatbot built on large language models, or with a self-chosen peer and no access to similar tools, to develop the research proposal that two markers scored (pp. 8-10, 12, 20). The paper also calls its design quasi-experimental (pp. 1, 3, 8) and describes no randomization method, which the form already records, but no page points to non-random grouping, so criterion 1 holds.
